verdict.rationale: Rive's model is that the editor output is the production artifact: the exported .riv file is loaded by open-source runtimes across web, mobile and game engines and wired to app state through data binding, so there is no handoff step. However, it does not generate application code or map design components to a codebase's own components; the shipped artifact is a runtime-rendered file, not code. missing for 10: component-to-code mappings into app frameworks, generated shippable source code (as opposed to a .riv asset), independent hands-on corroboration of the handoff-free workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, designs map to production code — component-to-code mappings or direct design-to-code output I can actually ship

citations.quote: What you build in the editor is what ships in your app, game, or website. No mockups, no prototypes, no handoff.
You can use the same exported file across supported runtimes, including web, mobile, game engines, and other platforms.
The Rive runtimes are open-source libraries that allow you to load and control your animations in apps, games, and websites.
When data changes, your scene updates automatically. Likewise, changes made in your scene can be written back to your data.
